theorem_title: Isolation of the reciprocal-triple gadget at 732
natural_language_statement:
Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $0<a<b<c\leq732$ and $a(b+c)=bc$. If at least one of $a,b,c$ belongs to $G=\{122,183,244,366,732\}$, then

$$
(a,b,c)\in\{(122,183,366),(183,244,732),(244,366,732)\}.
$$

This finite classification says that every forbidden reciprocal triple meeting the gadget lies wholly inside it. It supplies the isolation fact needed for the cardinality-preserving replacement.

theorem Erdos302Kernel.isolated_nat (a b c : Nat)
 (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hbc : b < c) (hc : c ≤ 732)
 (hrel : a * (b + c) = b * c)
 (hG : inGNat a || inGNat b || inGNat c) :
 (a = 122 ∧ b = 183 ∧ c = 366) ∨
 (a = 183 ∧ b = 244 ∧ c = 732) ∨
 (a = 244 ∧ b = 366 ∧ c = 732) := by sorry
